doc.title: Wilson "Chembo" Corniel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, November 15, 2019

title: Folkloric roots mixed with jazz in his group
summary: He takes rhythms from their folkloric roots and combines them with straight ahead jazz, giving his musicians space.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: What was that word you used?

Folkloric. Yes. You know so we try to take each rhythm from the ground and dissect it from there to bring it and mix it with the jazz. So we’ve got the jazz and we’ve got the roots, so my group is like that. We’re doing the straight ahead jazz with the bottom from Africa. So you know I give opportunities to my musicians all the time where I give them space, I lay out sometimes, and this is why with that comment you said before, I don’t hog up all the solos. You know it’s my band but I’m not going to be blowing all the time, but I’ve got these great musicians here and I utilize it.
